transcript.text: I'm 23, just quit what was probably the
best job I've ever had to go out on my
own and start my own business. Part of
me is fired up, part of me is terrified,
but should I actually be worried? And
what would you tell your 23-year-old
self before taking the leap?
>> You're not going to die. If you play out
your worst-case scenario, it's unlikely
that you're going to starve to death and
be homeless. And so, the true worst-case
scenario is that you sacrifice status,
which is really just a made-up
perception of yourself in other people's
mind, and you judging what they think
about you when they're not thinking
about you to begin with. If you're 23,
you have the highest risk-adjusted
return period of your life to make these
types of moves because if not now, then
when? Like when you have more
responsibility, when you have less time,
when you have a family, when you have
people who depend on you. You have none
of these obligations right now. And so,
if there's ever a time where you can
kind of take endless scratch-off tickets
from life, where even if it doesn't win,
the only thing you spent was time, and
you didn't lose, you learned, and you
just got better. And so, as long as you
know that your plan B is that you just
are going to keep trying, then plan A
and plan B merge and become the same
thing. Because at the end of the day,
failure and success are on the same
road. It's just that failure is an
earlier exit.
